intro:
HSR to West Kowloon; chartered van all day for photo stops, one area at a time
East Kowloon: Choi Hung Estate; through the tunnel to Quarry Bay: Monster Building
Wan Chai: Kam's roast goose at its 11:30 opening, Capital Café; Ding Ding tram west to Central
Central: escalator, Tai Cheong, Lan Fong Yuen; Peak Tram, Sky Terrace 428, Lugard Road, van down
Star Ferry to Tsim Sha Tsui: Mammy Pancake, Ocean Terminal Deck, Clock Tower, 1881 Heritage, Avenue of Stars
Optional: dinner at Tim Ho Wan in West Kowloon Station before clearance

items.title: K Hotel → Guangzhou South Station (广州南站)
Enter station, security check
items.note: Trains to Hong Kong require earlier arrival; 40 min should be allowed.
items.tip: Documents for entering Hong Kong and returning to the mainland must be carried; check once more before leaving.

items.title: HSR: Guangzhou South → Hong Kong West Kowloon (香港西九龙)
items.tip: HSR tickets should be bought as soon as sales open; year-end tickets sell out fast.

items.title: West Kowloon Station border clearance
items.note: Mainland exit and Hong Kong entry are both done inside the station.

items.title: Hong Kong route (chartered van)

route.title: West Kowloon Station → Choi Hung Estate (彩虹邨)
route.desc: Van, ~30 min
route.pick: West Kowloon Station private-car pick-up area; the level and exit should be confirmed with the driver by WhatsApp after clearance
route.drop: Near Choi Hung Estate, at a point the driver chooses

route.title: Choi Hung Estate (彩虹邨)
route.desc: Rainbow-painted blocks of an older public estate; the basketball court on the car-park roof is the best-known photo spot. 10 min, then on.
route.tip: This is a residential estate: photos should be taken quietly without blocking residents, and any no-photography notice on site should be followed.

route.title: Choi Hung → Quarry Bay (鲗鱼涌)
route.desc: Van, ~20 min via the Eastern Harbour Crossing, which comes out at Quarry Bay
route.pick: Where the group was dropped at Choi Hung
route.drop: Near Yick Cheong Building, King's Road

route.title: Monster Building (怪兽大厦)
route.walk: Into the courtyard from Yick Cheong Building, King's Road
route.desc: Five linked old residential blocks; from the courtyard the windows tower on every side. A filming location for Transformers: Age of Extinction. 10 min, then on.
route.tip: This is a residential estate: photos should be taken quietly without blocking residents, and any no-photography notice on site should be followed.

route.title: Quarry Bay → Wan Chai
route.desc: Van, ~15 min
route.pick: Where the group was dropped at Yick Cheong Building
route.drop: Near Kam's Roast Goose, 226 Hennessy Road, Wan Chai

route.title: Kam's Roast Goose (甘牌烧鹅)
route.desc: Michelin-starred roast goose; the goose leg is the order. Doors open at 11:30; queuing before then should get a first-round table.
route.tip: The queue grows fast after opening, so arrival should not be late.

food.name: Roast goose leg rice (烧鹅腿饭)
food.desc: Roast goose rice can be upgraded to the leg for a supplement

route.title: Capital Café (華星冰室)
route.desc: A well-known cha chaan teng: right after lunch a yuenyeung or milk tea is enough, with a pineapple bun if anyone is hungry; taken away if it is busy.

food.name: Yuenyeung, milk tea (鸳鸯、奶茶)
food.desc: Coffee mixed with milk tea, Hong Kong's signature drink

food.name: Scrambled-egg toast, pineapple bun (炒蛋多士、菠萝油)

route.title: Ding Ding tram (叮叮车)
route.walk: Back to Hennessy Road for a westbound tram (towards Central / Kennedy Town)
route.desc: Century-old tram; front seats on the upper deck give the best street view. ~25 min to Central; a Wise card or Apple Pay is tapped when getting off. The van goes ahead to Central.

route.title: Central–Mid-Levels Escalator (中环至半山自动扶梯)
route.walk: Off the tram in Central; ~5 min on foot to the escalator start on Queen's Road Central
route.desc: Billed as the world's longest covered outdoor escalator system; free. It runs uphill in the afternoon; two or three sections reach Lyndhurst Terrace.

route.title: Tai Cheong Bakery (泰昌饼家)
route.walk: At the Lyndhurst Terrace exit of the escalator
route.desc: Flaky egg tarts as an afternoon snack, eaten on the go. The stone steps of Pottinger Street (砵典乍街) are right at the corner, good for a quick photo.
route.tip: Pottinger Street is a stepped granite lane lined with stalls; the stones are uneven, so footing should be watched.

food.name: Lan Fong Yuen (兰芳园)
food.desc: 2 Gage St, ~1 min away; the original silk-stocking milk tea, taken away

food.name: LINLEE, Lyndhurst Terrace (LINLEE中环摆花街店)

route.title: Central → Peak Tram lower terminus (花园道山顶缆车总站)
route.desc: Van, ~10 min
route.pick: Around Lyndhurst Terrace / Hollywood Road, at a point the driver chooses
route.drop: Outside the Peak Tram lower terminus, Garden Road

route.title: Peak Tram (山顶缆车)
route.desc: Century-old funicular; the steep tilt on the way up is thrilling and memorable for kids. The right-hand side gives the city view.
route.tip: Afternoon queues can run over an hour, so a fast-track combo is essential (Peak Tram + Sky Terrace 428; the three-in-one adds Madame Tussauds). The 14:00 slot should be booked with arrival 15 min early; late arrivals may lose fast-track access. The ride is ~7 min. The van is taken down, so the return tram leg goes unused.

route.title: Madame Tussauds Hong Kong (杜莎夫人蜡像馆)
route.desc: Close-up photos with wax figures of stars and athletes; ~45 min. The times below assume it is skipped; if visited, everything after moves 45 min later.

route.title: Sky Terrace 428 (凌霄阁摩天台428)
route.walk: Top of the Peak Tower, by escalator
route.desc: A 360° deck 428 m above sea level over Victoria Harbour and Hong Kong Island; the classic skyline photo without a hill walk.
route.tip: The Peak is windier and colder than the city; a jacket should be brought.

food.name: Pacific Coffee, Peak Tower (Pacific Coffee凌霄阁)
food.desc: Local Hong Kong coffee chain; a short break for the adults

route.title: Lugard Road lookout (卢吉道观景台)
route.walk: ~10 min along flat, shaded Lugard Road from the Peak Tower
route.desc: A free lookout over Victoria Harbour and the Central towers; ~30 min there and back.

route.title: The Peak → Central Star Ferry Pier (中环天星码头)
route.desc: Van down, ~25 min; the downhill tram queue is avoided.
route.pick: The Peak Galleria car park; the exact spot should be agreed with the driver

route.title: Star Ferry: Central → Tsim Sha Tsui (天星小轮)
route.desc: Century-old ferry; ~15–20 min including the wait, across Victoria Harbour with the skyline on both sides. Tickets are bought by card at the pier's self-service machines.

route.title: Mammy Pancake (媽咪雞蛋仔)
route.walk: At the Tsim Sha Tsui Star Ferry Pier, off the boat
route.desc: Egg waffles listed in the Michelin street food guide, crisp outside and soft inside; an afternoon snack on the go.

food.name: Egg waffle (鸡蛋仔)
food.desc: Original is the classic; chocolate and other flavours too

route.tip: Small stalls like this may take only cash or Octopus; card or Apple Pay should be checked first, and the stop skipped if neither works.

route.title: Ocean Terminal Deck (海运大厦观景台)
route.walk: ~8 min, indoors through Harbour City to the end of Ocean Terminal
route.desc: A free harbourside rooftop facing Victoria Harbour and Hong Kong Island; afterwards the route heads east without turning back.

route.title: Tsim Sha Tsui Clock Tower (尖沙咀钟楼)
route.walk: ~8 min back to beside the Star Ferry pier
route.desc: The century-old clock tower left from the former Kowloon–Canton Railway terminus; a quick harbourside photo.

route.title: 1881 Heritage (前水警总部)
route.desc: The former Marine Police Headquarters; its colonial lawns and arcades photograph well, and a free Christmas installation is usually up at year end.
route.tip: This year's Christmas installation has not been announced; what is on show should be checked on the day.

route.title: Avenue of Stars (星光大道)
route.desc: The harbourfront promenade with the Bruce Lee statue, facing the island skyline; close to sunset, the light is at its best.

route.title: Tsim Sha Tsui → West Kowloon Station
route.desc: Van, ~20 min; evening traffic is expected.
route.pick: Near the Avenue of Stars (Salisbury Road); the exact spot should be agreed with the driver
route.drop: West Kowloon Station private-car drop-off area

items.note: The van is hired ~10:00–18:00 and the driver is contacted by WhatsApp; every pick-up and drop-off point is marked below. On the walking stretches the van goes ahead to the next pick-up point.
items.tip: Vans are usually hired by the hour; hours, harbour-tunnel tolls and parking should be agreed first. Many Central streets are no-stopping zones, so exact pick-up and drop-off points are set by the driver.

items.title: Dinner: Tim Ho Wan, West Kowloon Station (添好运西九龙站)
items.note: On level B1M of West Kowloon Station, before clearance. If taken, clearance and the train move ~50 min later, with the hotel reached ~21:10.
items.tip: Payment methods should be checked in store (review sites list Visa, Mastercard and Apple Pay).

food.name: Tim Ho Wan, West Kowloon Station (添好运西九龙站)
food.desc: Dim sum chain recognised by Michelin

food.name: Baked BBQ pork buns (酥皮焗叉烧包)
Shrimp siu mai, har gow (鲜虾烧卖、虾饺)
Pig liver rice roll (黄沙猪润肠)
food.desc: Strong flavour; for the adults to try

items.title: HSR: West Kowloon → Guangzhou South
items.note: ~50 min; times follow the ticket booked.

items.title: Dinner: near the hotel
items.tip: Skipped if dinner was taken at West Kowloon Station; otherwise dinner is late and a snack on the train helps.

notice: No Octopus card or coins needed. Ding Ding tram: a Wise card or Apple Pay is tapped when getting off; adult HK$3.3, child HK$1.6. Star Ferry: tickets are bought by card or QR at the pier's self-service machines; weekday adult HK$5.0, child HK$2.9. Both rides total HK$8.3 per adult and HK$4.5 per child. Foreign cards may incur cross-border fees.
